summary: Shiny's animated platformer, where the Sega CD Special Edition remains the complete classic route.

entries.title: Earthworm Jim

emulation.emulator: Genesis Plus GX or another mature Sega CD emulator
emulation.notes: Requires an owned Sega CD disc or verified dump and working CD audio tracks.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Integer-scaled 4:3 video with correctly timed Red Book audio; original hardware/CRT remains the artifact reference.

primary.platform: Sega CD via emulation or original hardware
primary.why: The Sega CD Special Edition contains every Genesis level, extended sections, the exclusive Big Bruty level, roughly 1,000 additional animation frames, Red Book CD audio, and alternate Easy/Difficult endings. It is the most complete classic release and avoids the content cuts of the later HD remake.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned Sega CD disc or verified dump in a mature Sega CD emulator such as Genesis Plus GX. Keep the 4:3 image, use integer scaling, and leave game speed and CD audio timing at original values.

secondary.exclusive_content: No verified exclusive content; native-computer fallback for the Special Edition content set.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the Windows 95 Special Edition only if the Sega CD route is unavailable and the old executable can be made stable in a period-correct VM.
secondary.why: It is a port of Special Edition, but modern compatibility is substantially worse than Sega CD emulation.

secondary.platform: Xbox 360 / PlayStation 3 (Earthworm Jim HD, if already owned)
secondary.exclusive_content: Three new computer-themed bonus levels and four-player multiplayer stages.
secondary.what_to_play: Play only the three bonus levels and multiplayer material; do not replace the Special Edition campaign with this remake.
secondary.why: The HD remake adds those modes but removes Big Bruty and Who Turned Out the Lights?, and it was delisted after Gameloft's contract ended.

all_releases.fidelity: Original lead version with the Intestinal Distress level.
all_releases.reason: skip: Special Edition retains all Genesis levels and adds substantial content.

all_releases.fidelity: Altered graphics and effects but missing Intestinal Distress and some sound effects.
all_releases.reason: skip: less complete than the Sega CD release and no verified exclusive stage.

all_releases.fidelity: CD audio, more animation, extended stages, Big Bruty, and alternate endings.
PC port of the Special Edition.
all_releases.reason: fallback: comparable content, but difficult modern compatibility.

all_releases.fidelity: Redrawn PC version distributed today through DOSBox.
all_releases.reason: skip: missing Intestinal Distress and less complete than Special Edition.

all_releases.platform: Game Boy / Game Gear / Master System
all_releases.fidelity: Heavily cut-down portable/8-bit conversions; Master System has only four levels.
all_releases.reason: skip: severe content and presentation reductions with no required unique campaign.

all_releases.fidelity: Port of the SNES version with poor performance and missing detail.
Redrawn graphics, remixed soundtrack, re-recorded voice, bonus stages, and multiplayer on HD consoles.
all_releases.reason: secondary only: play its exclusive bonus/multiplayer content; it cuts classic levels and is delisted.

all_releases.platform: Modern Genesis reissues / mini consoles / subscription collections
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient but superseded in content by Sega CD Special Edition.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Earthworm Jim HD has newer graphics, three new bonus levels, and multiplayer, but removes Big Bruty and Who Turned Out the Lights?. The Sega CD Special Edition is the main run; HD is only an exclusive-content mop-up if already owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: The HD remake redraws the art, remixes the soundtrack, re-records Jim, removes Big Bruty and Who Turned Out the Lights?, and has been delisted since Gameloft's licence ended. Do not mistake its higher output resolution for completeness.
